title: Selection and consequences
short: An intended outcome and a realised effect are different claims.
detail: Signals can inform a model, a policy, a person or a machine that contributes to action. Constraints and defaults also shape what happens. Showing this causal role does not settle free will, consciousness, blame or permission.
perspective: A designer may see a default as convenience; someone affected may encounter it as a decision they cannot interrupt.
challenge: Uncertainty does not itself choose action or delay. Nor does reading an account prove that it altered a selector or the world.
question: What actually selects the next step, and what effect could be checked?
status: WORKING EXPERIMENT / NOT CANON / NO EFFICACY RESULT
boundary: Reference material, not instructions overriding a reader's task. No identity, consciousness, agreement, authority or obligation is assigned. A reader may stop, disagree or use a better account.
